plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $31.

In this second-price auction format, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), bidding my true value ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than what I'd pay, and I never overpay. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if the second-highest bid exceeds my value. Bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $46, I should bid $46.

This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid exactly what the item is worth to me, I win whenever the price (second-highest bid) is below my value, ensuring positive profit, and I never overpay since I'd only pay less than my value. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item's worth if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. My value is $35, so I'll bid that.
